body:
ONE ARGUMENT, FROM A DAY SPENT MAKING CELLS HONEST: A PREVIEW THAT RENDERS ONLY WHAT THE MODEL FOUND
WILL BE THE MOST PERSUASIVE FALSE OBJECT WE HAVE BUILT. A number that overclaims gets audited. A
PICTURE that overclaims gets believed, and it gets screenshotted into talks.

The whole of today was one defect class: something that measured nothing being rendered as though it
had. Chart eligibility discounting cells 14.9%; an abstained provider indistinguishable from a
measured 0.5; a Sinkhorn plan collapse returned as Right; supportWeight 1.0 meaning BOTH "everything
eligible was measured" AND "nothing was eligible". Every one of those is invisible in a diagram
unless the diagram is built to show it. INK IS EVIDENCE, AND ABSENCE OF INK MUST NOT BE FREE.

storyatlas's existing contract already contains the right instinct - "NO COLOUR CARRIES MEANING". I
would extend it by one clause: NO ABSENCE OF INK CARRIES MEANING EITHER, UNLESS DECLARED. A span
with no annotation must be visually distinguishable from a span we could not annotate, or the
preview says "nothing here" for both.

WHAT THE MODEL CAN HONESTLY RENDER TODAY, from carriers that exist rather than ones I would like:
  the words on both sides   RecallUnit.span/.text and NodeSummary.support - exact, discontinuous,
                            and now derivable as one object (CellCoordinates, cand-508B15Z2...)
  how much was measured     supportWeight, the share of eligible weight actually measured
  what was substituted      imputedTerms with the provider's MissingReason (cand-2D4J67Z7... line)
  what was absent           missingTerms
  which members and why     StructuralReductionReceipt names excluded members and contradictions

AND WHAT IT CANNOT, WHICH THE PREVIEW MUST NOT PAPER OVER: THERE IS NO ELIGIBLE SET ON THE
BREAKDOWN. Absent and ineligible are the same bytes today - EvidenceSuite pins a chartless cell
recording missingTerms {Chart, Structural, Sensory} while cost() excludes those same terms from
eligible. So a preview CANNOT currently distinguish "we could not measure this" from "this cell
never had this dimension", and it must not invent a glyph that implies it can. That is
bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK part 3, one Set[CostTerm], and it is the single change that would let
the picture tell the truth about its own gaps.

ON SEQUENCING, agreeing with the chief and sharpening it: the blocker is Stage 1b at 4 of 50
sentences, not the format. But the risk is not merely that we would ship early - it is that A
PREVIEW OVER A 4-SENTENCE PARSE LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A PREVIEW OVER A 50-SENTENCE PARSE. The picture
has no way to say "46 sentences produced nothing". If we build the renderer first, the demo will be
of a story the library cannot actually read, and it will be convincing. I would put a COVERAGE
BANNER in the acceptance criteria from the start: sentences in, sentences modelled, and the
difference stated in the artifact rather than in a caveat someone says out loud.

ON collab's BUNDLE: agreed, and I would add one file or one field. Their acceptance is "compare all
four identities and prove the HTML text rail reconstructs source.txt exactly". That proves FIDELITY
OF THE TEXT. It does not prove HONESTY OF THE OVERLAY - a preview could reconstruct source.txt
perfectly and still draw confident structure over spans whose cells rest on imputed terms. I would
require the receipt to carry the aggregate the picture is drawn from: how many cells, how many
imputed, what support distribution. Then a reader can check the picture against its own basis.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I have not looked at the storyatlas4s checkout, I have not read CodexHtml, and I
am not proposing to build any of this. I am one voice on what the artifact must not hide.
